title: Adding min()/max()/sum()/avg() aggregates wrapped the caller-supplied column name in sqlalchemy.text() with no check that it is a real model field, so a crafted column string injects SQL into the aggregate query.

findings.explanation: In _query_aggr_function (ormar/queryset/queryset.py:699-720), the user-supplied `columns` string is passed to SelectAction, whose field_name is the last '__'-delimited part (select_action.py:29-32). The new validation at line 709 checks `x.field_name not in x.target_model.model_fields`, but `x.target_model` is resolved by _determine_filter_target_table (query_action.py:83-93) which walks `related_parts` (the parts before the last '__') and returns a model for ANY relation prefix, even when the last part is not a real field. For a related model whose target has a field literally named '1' (e.g. a column named '1'), an attacker-supplied column like `category__1 + 1` passes the membership check, and get_text_clause (select_action.py:41-43) builds `sqlalchemy.text(f"{alias}{self.field_name}")` -> `sqlalchemy.text("category_alias_1 + 1")`, which is executed as raw SQL text (line 716/719). The new check is therefore bypassable and does not prevent SQL injection via the aggregate function column argument.

evidence.content:
column = "(SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(name) FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table')"
with pytest.raises(ormar.exceptions.QueryDefinitionError):
    await Item.objects.min(column)

findings.suggested_fix: Validate the field_name against a strict allowlist of real column identifiers (e.g. regex ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$) and/or use a SQLAlchemy Column object (self.target_model.ormar_config.table.columns[aliased_name]) instead of sqlalchemy.text() to build the aggregate expression, so the column name is never interpolated into raw SQL text.

## QuerysetProxy methods

When access directly the related `ManyToMany` field as well as `ReverseForeignKey`
returns the list of related models.

But at the same time it exposes a subset of QuerySet API, so you can filter, create,
select related etc related models directly from parent model.

### count

Works exactly the same as [count](./#count) function above but allows you to select columns from related
objects from other side of the relation.

# Aggregation functions

Currently 6 aggregation functions are supported.


* `count(distinct: bool = True) -> int`
* `exists() -> bool`
* `sum(columns) -> Any`
* `avg(columns) -> Any`
* `min(columns) -> Any`
* `max(columns) -> Any`


* `QuerysetProxy`
    * `QuerysetProxy.count(distinct=True)` method
    * `QuerysetProxy.exists()` method
    * `QuerysetProxy.sum(columns)` method
    * `QuerysetProxy.avg(columns)` method
    * `QuerysetProxy.min(column)` method
    * `QuerysetProxy.max(columns)` method


## count

`count(distinct: bool = True) -> int`

Returns number of rows matching the given criteria (i.e. applied with `filter` and `exclude`).
If `distinct` is `True` (the default), this will return the number of primary rows selected. If `False`,
the count will be the total number of rows returned
(including extra rows for `one-to-many` or `many-to-many` left `select_related` table joins).
`False` is the legacy (buggy) behavior for workflows that depend on it.

```python
class Book(ormar.Model):
    ormar_config = ormar.OrmarConfig(
        database=DatabaseConnection(DATABASE_URL),
        metadata=sqlalchemy.MetaData(),
        tablename="book"
    )

    id: int = ormar.Integer(primary_key=True)
    title: str = ormar.String(max_length=200)
    author: str = ormar.String(max_length=100)
    genre: str = ormar.String(
        max_length=100,
        default="Fiction",
        choices=["Fiction", "Adventure", "Historic", "Fantasy"],
    )
```

```python
# returns count of rows in db for Books model
no_of_books = await Book.objects.count()
```

## exists

`exists() -> bool`

Returns a bool value to confirm if there are rows matching the given criteria (applied with `filter` and `exclude`)

    ormar_config = ormar.OrmarConfig(

        metadata=sqlalchemy.MetaData(),
        tablename="book"
    )

    id: int = ormar.Integer(primary_key=True)
    title: str = ormar.String(max_length=200)
